They often have to attend press conferences after events in which they have taken part as a condition of the contract they have with the event organisers, in whose interests it is to keep the media happy. They also make public appearances, which usually include media opportunities of some sort, in support of sponsors who are paying them for the publicity they attract. A good play offers the audience not only entertainment but substance; to engage our attention, a play must first entertain, but to hold our interest, it must have content as well. A play that merely entertains becomes less interesting over time; a play that attempts to educate without entertaining bores.
